title: She was doing everything right…
paragraphs:
She was doing everything right…
and still missed what mattered most.

Martha was moving.
Mary was still.
In Luke 10:38–42, the house is full, the pressure is real, and expectations are loud. Martha is serving, hustling, carrying the weight of responsibility. Plates. Preparations. Perfection.
And then—she snaps.
“Lord, don’t You care?”

That line doesn’t come from laziness.
It comes from overload.

From doing so much for Jesus…
that she stopped being with Him.
But here’s what we miss—

Martha wasn’t rebuked for serving.
She was corrected for being consumed.
“You are anxious and troubled about many things…”

Not evil things.
Not sinful things.
Just… too many things.
Meanwhile, Mary chose something radical.
She sat.

At His feet.
Eyes locked.
Heart open.
Noise silenced.
And Jesus says something that cuts through centuries:
“Mary has chosen the better part…”

Not the easier part.
The better part.

Stillness isn’t weakness.
It’s warfare.

Because the enemy doesn’t just tempt you with sin—
he distracts you with busyness.

So you look productive…
but feel empty.

You look faithful…
but feel far.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Jesus doesn’t shame Martha.
He invites her.

Away from anxiety.
Back to intimacy.

Because the Gospel isn’t: “Do more for God.”
It’s: “Come be with Me.”

Before the cross, before the resurrection, even here—
Jesus was already restoring distracted hearts.
And at the cross, He finished it.

Your worth is not in your workload.
Your acceptance is not in your activity.
Your peace is not in your performance.
It’s in Christ alone.
So pause.
Sit.
Listen.

He’s not asking for more effort.
He’s asking for your attention.

From anxiety to intimacy—
because Jesus rewrites everything.
